systemIntro.nervous-central: The central nervous system includes the brain and spinal cord. It interprets the senses, forms memories, and coordinates decisions and movement. It also regulates many automatic functions throughout the rest of the body.
systemIntro.cardiovascular: The cardiovascular system moves blood around the body. The heart sends oxygen, nutrients and hormones to the tissues and brings waste back. That steady flow lets the other organs keep working.
systemIntro.respiratory: The respiratory system brings air into the lungs and removes carbon dioxide. Nasal passages, bronchi and lungs filter, warm and distribute the air. Oxygen then enters the blood so cells can produce energy.
systemIntro.digestive: The digestive system turns food into nutrients the body can use. Mouth, stomach, intestines and pancreas work together to break down, absorb and eliminate. Without that chain, the other organs would lack fuel.
systemIntro.hepatic: The liver is the core of the hepatic system. It processes what arrives from digestion, makes proteins, and helps clear the blood of substances the body no longer needs. It also produces bile, which helps digest fats.
systemIntro.renal: The renal system filters the blood and regulates water and salts. The kidneys remove waste in urine and keep the internal balance. That constant cleanup protects the rest of the organs.
systemIntro.immune: The immune system identifies what does not belong and organizes a defense. The spleen filters the blood and takes part in that response. That helps the body react to infections and other threats.
systemIntro.reproductive: The reproductive system produces sex cells and hormones that influence development and the rest of the body. This atlas shows ovaries and testes as reference structures. It also takes part in hormonal balance, beyond reproduction itself.
systemIntro.integumentary: The integumentary system is the body’s covering. Skin protects, helps regulate temperature and senses touch. Teeth, included here as associated structures, take part in the first stage of eating.
systemIntro.sensory: The sensory system gathers information from the surroundings so the brain can interpret it. In this atlas the focus is on the eyes and vision. Clear sight depends on those structures and on their link with the nervous system.
systemIntro.endocrine: The endocrine system sends chemical messages — hormones — through the blood. It regulates metabolism, growth, stress and other slower rhythms of the body. Unlike a nerve signal, these messages take longer, but they can reach many organs at once.
systemIntro.nervous-peripheral: The peripheral nervous system is the network of nerves outside the brain and spinal cord. It carries information from skin, muscles and organs inward, and returns orders for movement or automatic adjustment. It is the wiring that connects the body with the central nervous system.
